raw_response:
Let me think this through like I always do.

My land is 4.1 mu, not much. I been farming 25 years. Cotton is my money crop — that is what pays. I put most land to cotton, about 2.5 mu. The other 1.6 mu I do wheat in winter then maize after wheat come off in June. Wheat flour feeds my family, maize I sell some and keep some. This is what my father did, what my neighbors do.

**Cotton (2.5 mu):** I buy Bt seed from the dealer in town. Everyone buys that one now — the bollworm don't eat it so bad. Before planting I plough deep, turn the soil good. I put 2 bags compound fertilizer (15-15-15) each mu as base, that's 100 jin. Then when the cotton start flowering I topdress urea, about half a bag per mu, maybe a bit more. I rather put too much than lose bolls. Water from my well 3 times — once after planting, once at flowering, once when bolls filling. Spray pesticide 5 times for aphids and bollworm, even with Bt seed you still get aphids bad. Last year I got about 250 jin seed cotton per mu, I hope same this year.

**Wheat (1.6 mu):** I plant after maize come off in October. Improved seed from dealer, not the old kind. One bag diammonium phosphate as base, then topdress urea one bag at jointing. Water 4 times — winter water, green-up, jointing, filling. Spray twice for aphid and rust. Rotary tiller do the ground, cheaper than plough. Expect maybe 400 jin per mu.

**Maize (1.6 mu):** After wheat harvest I direct-seed right into the stubble, no plough. Hybrid seed, everyone use hybrid now. Base fertilizer compound 1 bag, then urea topdress at knee-high. Water 2 times if rain short. Spray 2 times. Get maybe 500 jin per mu.

Money is tight with 4 people in the house. But cotton is worth it and I cannot skimp or the bolls don't fill.
